## Election reform push and the Iran war narrative (February 2026)

In February 2026, Trump pressed publicly for the elimination of mail-in voting, asking, "Why would you want mail-in ballots if you know it's corrupt? It's a corrupt system."[{N}] A Politico report summarized by the Badlands Brief found Republicans in [[congress|Congress]] largely ignoring the call, with members offering qualified or contrary positions on [[mail-in-voting|mail-in voting]].[{N}] Election-related legislation was passing the House but was expected to stall in the [[senate|Senate]].[{N}] [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] questioned why the coordinated cabinet-level reform push began only in the midterm election year, offering possible sequencing explanations while concluding that the most logical outcome was "another fake election."[{N}]

The same edition reported Israeli media claims that Trump was weighing US military strikes on [[iran|Iran]], reportedly telling aides action could occur "as soon as Saturday," even as he remained publicly steadfast that a deal could be reached.[{N}] [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] argued Trump was being pushed toward war by external forces — [[israel|Israel]], the military-industrial complex, and domestic political actors — and that [[vladimir-putin|Vladimir Putin]]'s entry into the field was the principal counterweight.[{N}]

The Brief also credited Trump with deliberately constructing the American conversation about Israel and Zionism: appointing [[mike-huckabee|Mike Huckabee]] as ambassador as his first major appointment, which enraged [[nick-fuentes|Nick Fuentes]] and the Groypers, and then defending [[tucker-carlson|Tucker Carlson]]'s decision to interview Fuentes on free-information grounds.[{N}] Separately, [[new-york-times|The New York Times]] revived scrutiny of Trump's ties to [[jeffrey-epstein|Jeffrey Epstein]] and to [[howard-lutnick|Howard Lutnick]], lamenting that the fallout had not reached the White House.[{N}]

## February 2026 strike speculation and trilateral naval drills

In February 2026, Israeli news reports said President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] was considering possible US military strikes against Iran, reportedly telling aides action could occur "as soon as Saturday," according to Israeli media citing "sources familiar with the matter."[{N}] Other anonymous Israeli officials quoted in several outlets said US action could take place "within days."[{N}] The [[israel-defense-forces|Israel Defense Forces]] assessed that Iran would likely direct retaliation at [[israel|Israel]] if the United States struck, and were reportedly preparing for retaliation scenarios affecting Israeli territory.[{N}]

No public announcement of an authorized strike, declaration of war, or confirmed US military action existed at the time.[{N}] [[new-york-times|The New York Times]] reported a sudden US military buildup in the region.[{N}]

As tensions escalated, [[russia|Russia]], Iran and [[china|China]] launched joint naval drills in the Gulf of Oman and near the [[strait-of-hormuz|Strait of Hormuz]] as part of the recurring [[maritime-security-belt|Maritime Security Belt]] exercises, a trilateral series held since 2019.[{N}]

The Badlands Brief traced the war narrative to an [[axios|Axios]] story by [[barak-ravid|Barak Ravid]], subsequently amplified by [[israel-hayom|Israel Hayom]].[{N}] [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] argued Trump was being pushed into the conflict by Israeli and military-industrial pressure and cited former Israeli prime minister [[naftali-bennett|Naftali Bennett]]'s remark that "they are never going to love us, so instead they should fear us" as evidence of the mindset driving escalation.[{N}]

First, Israeli media — including [[israel-hayom|Israel Hayom]], described as the country's largest online publication — reported that US strikes on [[iran|Iran]] were imminent, with the [[israel-defense-forces|IDF]] assessing that Iranian retaliation would likely target Israeli territory.[{N}] [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] argued that President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] was being pushed into war by Israel and the military-industrial complex, and cited former prime minister [[naftali-bennett|Naftali Bennett]]'s statement that "they are never going to love us, so instead they should fear us."[{N}]

[[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] argued that President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]] had created the entire dialectic, beginning with the appointment of Huckabee — the first major appointment of the administration — as ambassador, a choice that "triggered [[nick-fuentes|Nick Fuentes]] and the Groypers into the stratosphere."[{N}] When Carlson later interviewed Fuentes and faced calls for censorship, Trump defended the principle that people should have access to all information and make up their own minds.[{N}] In this reading, Trump deliberately engineered the conditions for a public argument about Israel and Zionism.[{N}]

## Epstein files scrutiny and the Ravid critique (February 2026)

In February 2026, Bannon became a principal target of the media wave the Badlands Brief characterized as an operation against President [[donald-trump|Donald Trump]]'s closest allies.[{N}] Released Epstein materials showed what [[ashe-in-america|Ashe in America]] described as a seemingly trusted advisor relationship between Bannon and [[jeffrey-epstein|Jeffrey Epstein]], with messages that "appear damning" but which she argued were also intriguing and possibly not what they seem.[{N}] In her reading, Bannon presented as an "Epstein fan boy" ingratiating himself into the financier's inner circle before his alleged death, a relationship that produced a reported 50 hours of footage of Epstein telling Bannon "his side" of many stories.[{N}] Two of those hours had been released; Ashe reported they contained little discussion of sex trafficking or crimes against children and instead revealed Epstein's comfortable position among a tight-knit group of globalist bankers, with much of the footage concerning the 2008 financial collapse.[{N}] She suggested the remaining 48 hours, and even the first two, might furnish prosecutors probable cause to seize globalist assets, and withheld judgment on Bannon.[{N}]

In the same edition, Bannon publicly criticized [[axios|Axios]] reporter [[barak-ravid|Barak Ravid]] and his story claiming imminent US strikes on [[iran|Iran]].[{N}] [[burning-bright|Burning Bright]] defended Bannon as the author of some of Trump's most consequential speeches and as the singular MAGA voice who had accurately called out election-fraud machinery for a full decade before it became a palatable topic.[{N}]
